newsitem.title: JAPAN: Okinawans back move to cut U.S. forces - exit poll.
newsitem.headline: Okinawans back move to cut U.S. forces - exit poll.

text.p: Residents of the Japanese island of Okinawa on Sunday approved by a wide margin a measure aimed at reducing the massive U.S. military presence there, exit polls conducted by NHK television showed.
A "yes" vote, supported by Provincial Governor Masahide Ota, had been expected. But voter turnout, at an estimated 60 percent, was less than supporters had hoped for.
NHK gave no exact figures on the breakdown of the vote. It said the survey was based on interviews with some 2,200 voters.
Early official results representing five percent of the electorate showed the resolution gaining approval at an 8-1 ratio.
Officials said that hot, sunny weather and the strong likelihood of a victory for the anti-bases lobby in the non-binding referendum may have discouraged potential voters.

After years of simmering discord over the 40 U.S. bases on the island, occupying 20 percent of the total land, the issue has become one of the top political problems for Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
